name: diag_wood_axe
what: a wood axe: a broad wedge-shaped head of carved warm orange-brown wood with clear grain, crude and chunky, on a plain wooden handle, the head lashed on with tan cord. The handle runs along the canvas diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right; the axe head sits at the handle's top end and follows that diagonal: its cutting edge is a straight or gently curved line running perpendicular to the handle, from the upper left down to the lower right (along the canvas's other diagonal), never a vertical edge and never parallel to the canvas sides. Filling the canvas corner to corner The head is clearly an axe, not a hammer: a wedge that flares from a narrow neck at the handle to a wide curved cutting edge, about 12 px wide along the edge, carved wood grain running along it.

name: diag_diamond_axe
what: a diamond axe: a broad wedge-shaped head of faceted cyan diamond with teal shadows, white facet tips and one small sparkle, on a long handle wrapped in red-brown leather with gold cross-bands and a round gold pommel, a gold collar where head meets handle. The handle runs along the canvas diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right; the axe head sits at the handle's top end and follows that diagonal: its cutting edge is a straight or gently curved line running perpendicular to the handle, from the upper left down to the lower right (along the canvas's other diagonal), never a vertical edge and never parallel to the canvas sides. Filling the canvas corner to corner The head is a broad, heavy wedge of faceted diamond, as wide as an iron axe's, flaring from the collar to a wide cutting edge; not a thin blade, not a hoe or a pickaxe.
